title: Mild Chicken Sausage Rice Pot (Justin cut)
creator: Andy (one-pot sausage rice Short)
summary: Andy-style one-pot sausage rice: soffritto (onion/carrot/celery), sausage, paprika, Arborio, chicken stock, lid 20 min, spinach finish. Justin cut swaps spicy chorizo for mild chicken sausage or diced chicken breast, softens the paprika to a sweet pinch only, and offers a clear lower-carb half-rice path — still one pot.
whyItFits: Chicken night, weeknight easy, minimal dishes
Mild — no spicy chorizo heat, no smoked-paprika kick
High protein: mild chicken sausage or extra breast
Lower-carb option: half Arborio + riced cauliflower (or more chicken / less rice)
Spinach handful for volume and fiber

items: 1 celery stick, finely diced (optional — Andy skips if he doesn’t have it)
2 mild chicken sausages (~6–8 oz / 170–225 g), diced — not spicy chorizo
8–10 oz (225–280 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, diced (leaner / higher protein)
Pinch sweet paprika only (go easy — skip heavy smoked paprika kick)
500 ml chicken stock (or water in a pinch)

steps: Heat olive oil in a pot with a lid. Add onion, carrot, and celery with a pinch of salt; sauté a few minutes until softening. Add garlic; cook ~30–60 seconds.
Add diced mild chicken sausage or chicken breast. Cook until the sausage browns lightly or the breast is opaque on the outside.
Add a pinch of sweet paprika, salt, and pepper. Stir in the Arborio (full 120 g, or 60 g if doing the LC half-batch). Toast the rice 1–2 minutes, coating in the oil and fond.
Pour in 500 ml chicken stock. Bring to a light simmer, lid on, heat as low as it’ll go. Leave ~20 minutes (don’t stir constantly — this isn’t risotto labor).
If using riced cauliflower: for the half-rice path, fold it in during the last 5–8 minutes so it warms through without turning to mush. Add a splash more stock if the pot looks dry.
Lid off, heat up briefly. Add spinach, lid 60 seconds, stir through. Low another 60 seconds. Taste salt. Serve.
substitutions: No spice / mild: mild chicken sausage or plain breast only — not spicy chorizo. Sweet paprika pinch only; skip cayenne, chili flakes, and heavy smoked paprika.
Lower carb: half Arborio (60 g) + riced cauliflower; or more chicken / less rice overall. Still one pot.
Higher protein: prefer chicken breast path, or mild chicken sausage + a few extra ounces diced breast.
Celery: optional — skip if you don’t have it (Andy does the same).
Stock: chicken stock preferred; water works with a bit more salt.
Sweeteners: not needed here — savory dish. Save stevia / monk fruit / 0-sugar syrup for sauces elsewhere.
notes: Source: https://youtu.be/3hD36vDPqVI — Andy one-pot sausage rice.
Arborio isn’t soaked; toasting in the pot matters for texture.
Don’t crank smoked paprika — the mild cut lives or dies on that pinch staying sweet and light.
Leftovers reheat with a splash of stock; spinach will wilt further (fine).

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate for breast + half Arborio + cauliflower path per serving. Not lab-tested.

title: Mild Peanut Cucumber Chicken Salad (Justin cut)
creator: YouTube Shorts (viral high-protein chili peanut cucumber salad review)
summary: Viral high-protein chili peanut cucumber salad (~450 cal / ~40 g protein claimed) — shake-in-a-bowl format with cucumber, peanut butter, soy, garlic, cabbage, chicken, lime, and sesame. Justin cut drops chili oil, swaps honey for the sweetener kit, and keeps (or bumps) the chicken.
whyItFits: High protein chicken + peanut butter punch
Mild — no chili oil; sesame oil + lime/vinegar for brightness
Crunchy cucumber + cabbage keeps it light and lower-cal than creamy salads

items: 1 large cucumber, chopped (or smashed + chopped for more sauce cling)
18 g natural peanut butter (keep — worth it)
1–2 tsp sesame oil (instead of chili oil)
Tiny splash rice vinegar or extra lime (brightness without heat)
1–2 tsp 0-sugar simple syrup or a pinch monk fruit / stevia (instead of 10 g honey)
150–200 g cooked chicken breast, cubed or shredded
Optional: pinch salt if PB is unsalted; optional soft herbs (cilantro) if you like them

steps: Add cucumber, cabbage, and chicken to a large sealable bowl or container with a lid.
Add peanut butter, soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, vinegar or extra lime, sweetener kit, and lime juice.
Seal and shake hard until the peanut butter loosens into a glossy dressing and everything is coated. (Or stir vigorously if no lid.)
Top with sesame seeds. Eat right away for max crunch.
substitutions: No spice / mild: skip chili oil entirely; use sesame oil + lime/vinegar.
Sweeteners: 0-sugar simple syrup, monk fruit, or stevia instead of honey.
Extra protein: 180–200 g chicken; keep the 18 g PB.
Lower cal: measure PB carefully (18 g); use lean chicken breast; more cucumber/cabbage volume.
notes: Source: https://youtu.be/-25Z20zoHuA — viral chili peanut cucumber salad shake-bowl.
Chili oil is the only heat driver in the original — removing it is the whole mild cut.
Smash cucumber lightly before chopping so it soaks up dressing.
Best eaten fresh; cabbage softens if it sits overnight.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate for 1 bowl ~175 g chicken + 18 g PB, 0-cal sweetener, no chili oil. Not lab-tested.
